content.title: Italy holds off Puerto Rico rally, reaches WBC semifinals: Highlights
content.text: Updated March 14, 2026, 8:00 p.m. ETItaly is heading to the World Baseball Classic semifinals for the first time. And at this point, it’s pure folly to doubt that the Italians are merely espresso-chugging curiosities.Thanks to sterling relief pitching and two big innings, Italy took out Puerto Rico, 8-6, in the quarterfinal round at Houston’s Daikin Park on March 14. It’s the first time Italy has advanced out of the second or quarterfinal round, and with Team USA and Puerto Rico pelts on its wall, the targets only get bigger.Awaiting in the March 16 semifinal in Miami: The winner of defending champion Japan and Venezuela’s quarterfinal.Italy plays on because a rowdy opening few innings calmed down thanks to reliever Dylan DeLucia, who pitched four shutout innings and delivered a beleaguered Italy bullpen to the late innings. The Italians almost gave it all back in the eighth, when Matt Festa issued a pair of walks and Joe La Sorsa hit a batter.Christian Vazquez’s two-run single brought it to 8-6 – a lot different than 8-2 to begin the inning – but Red Sox right-hander Greg Weissert recorded the final two outs to end the eighth and pitched a scoreless ninth.The usual suspects also chipped in: Vinnie Pasquantino, Jac Caglianone and Dominic Canzone delivered RBI singles in a four-run first, and Andrew Fischer and J.J. D’Orazio hit consecutive two-run doubles in the fourth.Only avid hardball enthusiasts might have known those budding and future Major League Baseball stars. But the American-born and Italian native players have left their mark in this WBC.And the ride isn’t over yet.Puerto Rico's players stood and applauded the fans who jammed Daikin Park for this quarterfinal, the end of a wild ride that began with the roster's ravaging due to insurance issues. Yet Puerto Rico has never missed the quarterfinal round in the WBC, a streak it kept alive in 2026.They will go no further, though, falling just short against this event's newest blue blood.USA TODAY Sports provided live updates throughout the game: Italy vs. Puerto Rico highlights Puerto Rico rallies for four in eighth, pulls within 8-6 of ItalyItaly is just three outs away from reaching the World Baseball Classic semifinals. But the journey just got a lot more uncomfortable.Two walks, a hit batter and a wild pitch breathed life into a moribund Puerto Rico offense, and Christian Vazquez's two-run single keyed a startling four-run top of the eighth inning as the Boricua closed within 8-6 of Italy heading to the bottom of the eighth.Italy's Dylan DeLucia had shut out Puerto Rico from the third through seventh innings, handing an 8-2 lead to Matt Festa with just six outs to get.But Festa walked two and gave up a single, while Joe La Sorsa induced an RBI fielder's choice to make it an 8-3 game with one out. No problem, it seemed.But La Sorsa uncorked a wild pitch, allowing Emmanuel Rivera to score and make it an 8-4 game. Vazquez followed with a grounder through the right side to score two runs. And 8-2 was now 8-6.Greg Weissert, the Boston Red Sox right-hander, was summoned to put out the fire. And he struck out Willi Castro and, after a Darell Hernaiz single, induced a grounder to third from Nolan Arenado to end the threat.But the ninth inning just got a lot more interesting. Dylan DeLucia's sparkling relief outing gets Italy through sixthSurvival in a tournament like the World Baseball Classic requires gallant relief efforts from unexpected sources. In the quarterfinals against Puerto Rico, Italy got just that from Dylan DeLucia.After starter Sam Aldegheri got just four outs and reliever Alek Jacob got them out of the second inning, DeLucia took it from there for Italy. He pitched four shutout innings, giving up two hits, walking nobody and striking out three. It was a 4-2 Italy lead when he entered, and 8-2 heading to the seventh when he departed.The Cleveland Guardians Class AA starter has a 2.35 ERA in this WBC.Dan Altavilla created a first-and-third, no-out situation in the seventh, but a Darell Hernaiz strikeout keyed his escape, and Italy moved within six outs of advancing to the semifinals. Fan interferes, but Andrew Fischer, Italy extend lead to 8-2Italy got a huge piece of insurance, even with a little interference from a fan.Nursing a two-run lead with two outs and two on in the fourth inning, Fischer hooked a fly ball off Puerto Rican reliever Luis Quiñones into right center field, nearing the wall. But before the ball could strike or climb over the wall, an apparently non-partisan fan - clad in an official WBC shirt that would make Rob Lowe proud - made a nifty catch with his glove.The interference call was obvious, and Fischer, the 20th overall pick by the Brewers out of Tennessee in July, had a two-run double, his sixth and seventh runs batted in in this WBC.J.J. D'Orazio followed with a two-run double of his own, and Italy suddenly had an 8-2 lead entering the fifth inning.Reliever Eduardo Rivera comes up huge, keeps Puerto Rico closeEduardo Rivera has yet to make his major league debut. Yet he showed enough mettle in a huge spot to indicate that time might not be far away.The 6-7, 245-pound lefty, who has reached Class AA in the Red Sox system, inherited a two-out, one-on situation trailing Italy 4-2 in the bottom of the second and hulking Vinnie Pasquantino at the plate. Rivera won that battle with the Pasquatch, striking him out on a 98 mph fastball as Jakob Marsee stole second.After walking Dominic Canzone, the bases were loaded and slugger Jac Caglianone was up. Manager Yadier Molina went out for an extended mound visit, mulled a change, but kept the 22-year-old in.Wise move: Rivera punched out Caglianone on three pitches, the last a 98 mph fastball to leave the bases loaded.Rivera added a scoreless inning of work, pitching around a Dante Nori two-out single. It remains 4-2 heading to the fourth. Puerto Rico gets run back in second, but missed bigger chanceItaly swung the door open for Puerto Rico in the second inning, walking two batters and hitting two more, the latter Martín Maldonado with the bases loaded to make it a 4-2 game.Yet reliever Alek Jacob snuffed out the bases-loaded rally, striking out leadoff man Willi Castro and getting Darell Hernaiz on a grounder to short as Italy retains its lead heading to the bottom of the second.There was a bit of collateral damage for Italy: Starter Samuel Aldegheri was pulled from the game after walks to Heliot Ramos and Eddie Rosario and hitting Matthew Lugo on the foot. But Jacob did well to minimize the damage. Italy storms back, chases Seth Lugo for 4-1 lead after oneFirst, Seth Lugo got squeezed. Then he got tortured by Italy's irrepressible lineup.The Kansas City Royals starter issued a leadoff walk that was keyed by a clearly missed call by homeplate umpire Carlos Torres, then after a one-out free pass was peppered with RBI singles by Royals teammates Vinnie Pasquantino and Jac Caglianone and Mariners DH Dominic Canzone as Italy seized a 4-1 lead after one inning.After Caglianone's single, manager Yadier Molina lifted Lugo after recording just one out, giving up three runs and throwing 25 pitches. Lefty Jovani Moran came on to prevent more damage, but walked a batter and yielded J.J. D'Orazio's sacrifice fly for a 4-1 Italy lead after one. Willi Castro's leadoff homer stakes Puerto Rico to 1-0 leadPlantain Power is finally back.Puerto Rico hit just one home run in four pool play games - only Colombia, with zero, hit fewer - and forged its reputation on stout pitching entering the WBC quarterfinal against Italy. But in cozy Daikin Park in Houston, leadoff man Willi Castro wasted no time, hitting Sam Aldegheri's fourth pitch of the game for a home run to left field and a quick 1-0 Puerto Rico lead.Aldegheri settled down to retire the next three batters. And now Italy's powerful club - it hit 12 homers in pool play - is coming up.How to watch Puerto Rico vs Italy baseball gameTime: 3 p.m. ETTV channel: Fox Sports 1Live stream: FuboWatch WBC live on Fubo Italy lineup today vs. PRStarting pitcher: LHP Sam AldegheriSam Antonacci – 2BThomas Saggese – SSJakob Marsee – CFVinnie Pasquantino – 1BDominic Canzone – DHJac Caglianone – RFAndrew Fischer – 3BJ.J. It never happened before. People are talking about baseball. It never happened," Cervelli said. "They are excited. They love what's happening, and we've got to continue doing this, creating an impact. That was what we were looking for, make noise, and the guys they've been making noise.
